searchText: wow, finality 🥳 Awesome <@557201004060213248> did you bring your validators online ? He did: https://witti.beaconcha.in/validators/eth1deposits?q=0xeef4aB970751CA4F315FB1D9c61729949aBD29E7 yes, after the stack overflow patch from teku, we have finality again Nice > Also let's ask <@!97774605351010304> to clarify what the epoch % is in the block explorer <@!291925846556540928> it's the participation rate of the whole epoch <@!557201004060213248> is this art? boring 🙂 that long unfinalized period was a nice stress test Personally I appreciate the break so we can go apply the things we’ve learnt without discovering new things for a bit. But I think it would be worth having a testnet run for long enough for finality to be restored just through inactivity penalties. Nimbus seems to sync & keep in sync now on witti, no problems or excessive memory usage while syncing through the unfinalized period. Haven't tested validating yet though. I think we should discuss the inactivity penalty. It takes too long to kick inactive validators. They should be booted after 4 weeks. I don't think we have the patience to run such a testnet for a couple of months Doesn't the time required to kick them indirectly correlate with number of validators? Wouldn't it be much slower the more validators we have? It takes about 2.5 weeks to reduce those offline to 60% of their balance. This means that if 50% remain offline, then it takes about 2.5 weeks for the 50% online to become a 66% and start finalizing. If the amount offline is less than 50% then it takes less than the 2.5 weeks to get there The kick isn't what matters here it is the leak of funds in the 50% scenario, no one even has to get kicked (becuase the offline lost 40%, rather than the 50% (16 total ETH) required to kick them) when vals do get kicked for low balance, they do enter into the exit queue so if a lot of them get kicked at once, they won't quickly get out. But if there is still an inactivity leak, they will still continue to quadraticly increasingly lose capital > I don't think we have the patience to run such a testnet for a couple of months I think we can and should run some of these types of tests on the side rather than on user facing nets. In some of the stress tests we want to run, we want to reduce slot time aggressively (say 3 seconds), this would make the leak we are looking for happen in 4 or 5 days without adjusting constants. aha where do you get 2.5 weeks from? https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#rewards-and-penalties On witti we didn't see any exits and it's more than 3 weeks now The INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT equals INVERSE_SQRT_E_DROP_TIME**2 ... this validator never validated and his balance is 30 https://witti.beaconcha.in/validator/7 ah, so when there is no finality, penalties increase more and more offline penalties* well, we only lost finality for two days right so the "quadratic leak" was still ramping up `get_inactivity_penalty_deltas` this function serves to increasingly penalize those offline during a period of non-finality when there is finality and you are offline, you only stand to lose about as much as you could have made (if could make +10% over the course of a year, you could make -10%) ok. I'll continue observing this. I feel many were distracted by the Onyx launch this weekend. I'm happy we got back to 70% pariticipation. we can make a net with one node but just 50% of the vals and observe just to trigger this consensus path or make a net with 3-4 nodes (one each client) and 50% vals ok well, at least we should keep witti around even after altona launch continue to run a few nodes as users drop off each node that has vals that can continue forward will eventually finalize. I expect some optimizations for this scenario coming soon on some (e.g. teku) so not all of them will necessarily make it on v0.11 On some resource I read about that you guys are plan to setup specific testnet(s) for trying to break the chain? Sounds like such a testnet would be good for the issue you discussing. As <@!291925846556540928> wrote with low slottime. I don't know if it adds value (because you can off course setup in a small team or between implementers) but if those are public maybe some coordinated attacks (e.g. going offline) could be organized (on which ever vector). once we have testnets that we manage _not_ to break ... 🙂 Interestingly some of the things we learnt for teku in this round weren't just about the long non-finalization period but also about peer and REST API requests and the impact their demands had on resources. We wouldn't have hit those issues just syncing through the non-finalized period - you had to really live through it. So would be good to have a busy testnet that we deliberately break finality on at some point in the future. Based on current experience I suspect that may be unavoidable anyway...

I think we can and should run some of these types of tests on the side rather than on user facing nets. In some of the stress tests we want to run, we want to reduce slot time aggressively (say 3 seconds), this would make the leak we are looking for happen in 4 or 5 days without adjusting constants.
